newsitem.title: USA: Arraignment in Cosby son's murder postponed.
newsitem.headline: Arraignment in Cosby son's murder postponed.

text.p: The arraignment of an 18-year-old Russian emigre in the murder of entertainer Bill Cosby's son was postponed for two weeks on Friday, apparently because of confusion over who would defend the suspected killer.
Earlier, charges of murder with special circumstances were filed against Mikhail Markhasev, meaning he could receive the death penalty if found guilty of shooting Ennis Cosby.
Judge Michael Kellogg gave no reason for postponing the arraignment until March 28, but local television said there appeared to be confusion over which defence lawyer would represent Markhasev.
The arraignment had initially been delayed after lunch when Kellogg said he was waiting for a defence attorney. But when the lawyer arrived he did not immediately appear with the suspect.
Instead Markhasev was represented by private attorney Darren Kavinoky. Kellogg conferred with both sides in chambers before announcing the postponement.
The suspect, wearing a white T-shirt and looking sullen, appeared briefly in the courtroom and answered "yes," when the judge asked him if he agreed to the postponement.
He stood with hands in pockets behind a glass partition and surrounded by court officers. There did not appear to be any family members in the courtroom in the downtown Criminal Courts Building.

Markhasev, who came to the United States eight years ago from the former Soviet Union, was charged with one count of murder, one of attempted robbery and one of using a firearm in the commission of a crime. Cosby was shot once in the head while changing a tire near a freeway off-ramp.

Prosecutors, who were represented in court by deputy District Attorney Anne Ingalls, made clear they wanted the death penalty by adding the "special circumstances" charge of attempted robbery to the murder and weapons charges.
Because of the special circumstances, no bail was set and Markhasev will remain in custody until the March 28 hearing.
Cosby, 27, the only son of TV star and comedian Bill Cosby, was gunned down in the early hours of Jan. 16 while changing a tire on his luxury Mercedes car.
At the time of the murder police said there was no indication anything had been stolen from Cosby, leading to speculation the graduate student may have been set up.
However Los Angeles police chief Willie Williams said on Thursday the evidence suggested a random crime.
He also discounted reports that the killing was carried out by a Russian mob.
